title: Pizza history: AI agent’s cardless purchase is a first for UK
summary: Papa John’s order was made without sharing bank security details – tech that could revolutionise shopping Retailers enter the unknown with AI shopping assistants on Black Friday An order of Papa John’s margherita pizzas has become the first purchase in the UK to be made using an AI agent using cardless payment technology. The order of nine mini pizzas was made as part of the Financial Conduct Authority’s (FCA) regulated sandbox trials to test the technology, using Lloyds Bank and payment specialist TrueLayer. title: Banks may pass on £1.5bn tax rise to customers, warns Bank of England chief
summary: Big lenders will aim to ‘protect their earnings’ amid temporary increase in corporation tax surcharge, says Andrew Bailey Business live – latest updates The governor of the Bank of England has warned that banks could look to pass on the £1.5bn cost of Labour’s increase to tax on their profits amid pressure on household finances. John Healey, the chancellor, used his first budget last month to temporarily increase the bank corporation tax surcharge from 3% to 6% for a 15 month period from January, with the proceeds to be used to fund “breathing space” measures for households. title: Water firms to identify 250,000 vulnerable households in England eligible for discounts
summary: Department for Work and Pensions to provide data about households missing out on WaterSure support scheme Water companies will use government data to identify as many as 250,000 vulnerable households in England eligible for discounts, after criticism that not enough people are aware of the £428 support for their annual bills. The Department for Work and Pensions will provide information to identify and contact a quarter of a million households who are missing out on support to which they are entitled under the WaterSure scheme . The justice minister Sarah Sackman told parliament on Friday that Labour would support a private member’s bill sponsored by the Conservative MP Sir John Whittingdale, who is spearheading the latest attempt to bring in anti-Slapp measures. title: Labour’s split over Rosebank oilfield exposed by letter from nearly 100 MPs

Labour’s internal divisions over the giant Rosebank oilfield have spilled into the open, with nearly 100 Labour MPs – including a handful of frontbenchers – writing to the prime minister to express their opposition to the project. Ninety-two backbenchers and at least four frontbenchers have signed a letter to Andy Burnham urging him not to let his ministers approve the scheme for the biggest undeveloped field in UK waters. title: Up to 1.4m UK workers risk missing out on zero-hours shake-up, say unions
summary: Andy Burnham is warned against calls from bosses to water down employment rights legislation Andy Burnham is being warned that 1.4 million workers will be at risk of being stuck in insecure jobs if a forthcoming ban on zero-hours contracts is watered down.
